description: Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled is a quintessential Indian dish, featuring succulent chicken marinated in a rich blend of yogurt and aromatic spices, then cooked to perfection over hot coals. The charcoal grilling imparts an irresistible smoky flavor and a beautiful charred exterior, creating a truly aromatic and flavorful experience. This vibrant dish is a feast for both the eyes and the palate, perfect for any special dinner.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken for First Marinade
instructions.text: Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them completely dry. Make deep gashes on the chicken pieces to allow the marinade to penetrate. In a large bowl, apply the first marinade by rubbing lemon juice and salt all over the chicken. Let it rest for 15-20 minutes.

instructions.title: Prepare the Second Marinade
instructions.text: In a separate bowl, combine the hung yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, black pepper powder, and mustard oil. If using, add a pinch of red or orange food color for that classic Tandoori look. Mix everything well until you have a smooth, thick paste.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: Add the chicken pieces from the first marinade into the bowl with the second marinade. Ensure each piece is thoroughly coated with the spice-yogurt mixture, working the marinade into the gashes. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, for best flavor absorption.

instructions.title: Prepare the Charcoal Grill
instructions.text: About 30 minutes before grilling, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the charcoal to create medium-hot heat. Once the coals are glowing and covered with a fine grey ash, the grill is ready. Lightly oil the grill grates to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Grill the Tandoori Chicken
instructions.text: Place the marinated chicken pieces directly on the hot grill grates. Grill for about 8-10 minutes on each side, turning occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through and has a beautiful charred exterior. The internal temperature should reach 165F (74C).

instructions.title: Baste and Finish
instructions.text: During the last 5-7 minutes of grilling, generously baste the chicken pieces with melted butter or oil. This will add moisture and enhance the flavor and shine. Continue grilling until the chicken is tender, juicy, and perfectly smoky with slightly crisp edges.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Remove the Tandoori Chicken from the grill and let it rest for a few minutes. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and serve immediately with lemon wedges, onion rings, mint chutney, or a fresh green salad. Enjoy the authentic flavors!

tips: For truly authentic flavor, ensure your yogurt is thick and drained of excess water. Hung yogurt provides a richer, more concentrated marinade that adheres better to the chicken.
Do not skip the double marination process. The initial lemon and salt marinade tenderizes the chicken, while the second yogurt-spice marinade infuses deep, complex flavors.
Maintain a medium-hot charcoal grill. If the grill is too hot, the outside will burn before the inside cooks. If too cool, the chicken will dry out. Basting regularly helps keep it moist.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the vibrant streets of India right in your backyard! The aroma of sizzling spices, the smoky char, and the tender, juicy meat of Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled is an experience that transcends mere eating – it's a celebration of flavors. While traditionally cooked in a scorching clay tandoor oven, achieving that authentic taste and texture at home is not only possible but incredibly rewarding with a charcoal grill. This guide will walk you through creating a show-stopping Indian dinner recipe that will impress every palate and leave a lasting impression.

## What is Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled?
Tandoori Chicken is one of India's most iconic dishes, recognized globally for its distinctive red hue, smoky flavor, and succulent texture. At its heart, it's chicken marinated in yogurt and a potent blend of spices, then traditionally cooked at very high temperatures in a cylindrical clay oven called a tandoor. The tandoor imparts a unique smoky char while keeping the chicken incredibly moist inside. When we talk about Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled, we're aiming to replicate this magic using a home charcoal grill. The intense heat from the charcoal and the direct flame contact mimic the tandoor's environment, infusing the chicken with an irresistible smoky depth that oven-baked versions simply can't match. The marination is key, tenderizing the meat and allowing the spices to penetrate deeply, creating layers of flavor that burst with every bite. This method not only delivers on taste but also offers that beautiful, slightly charred exterior that is the hallmark of truly authentic tandoori preparations.

## Ingredients You Need
To create this magnificent Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled, gather the following:

For the Chicken:
*   1.5 kg (approx. 3.3 lbs) whole chicken, cut into 8 pieces (or 6-8 chicken thighs/drumsticks)
*   2 tablespoons lemon juice
*   1 teaspoon salt
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder

For the Marinade:
*   1 cup full-fat plain Greek yogurt (or hung curd, where excess whey is drained)
*   2 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste (equal parts fresh ginger and garlic, crushed)
*   2 tablespoons Kashmiri chili powder (for color and mild heat; adjust to taste)
*   1 tablespoon ground cumin
*   1 tablespoon ground coriander
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon black pepper
*   1/4 teaspoon red food color (optional, for authentic red hue)
*   1 tablespoon mustard oil (or any neutral oil like vegetable/canola)
*   1 teaspoon dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi), crushed (optional, but highly recommended for authentic flavor)
*   Salt to taste

## Step-by-Step Instructions
1.  **Prepare the Chicken:** Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them completely dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, make deep gashes (2-3 per piece) on the chicken. This allows the marinade to penetrate deeply.
2.  **First Marinade:** In a large bowl, combine the lemon juice, 1 teaspoon salt, and turmeric powder. Rub this mixture all over the chicken pieces, ensuring it gets into the gashes. Let it rest for 15-20 minutes. This initial marinade helps tenderize the chicken and adds a foundational layer of flavor.
3.  **Prepare the Second Marinade:** In a separate bowl, combine the Greek yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri chili powder, ground cumin, ground coriander, garam masala, black pepper, red food color (if using), mustard oil, and crushed kasoori methi. Mix well until all spices are evenly distributed. Taste and adjust salt if needed.
4.  **Marinate the Chicken:** Add the chicken pieces to the second marinade, ensuring each piece is thoroughly coated. Use your hands to massage the marinade into the chicken and the gashes. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight (12-24 hours) for the best flavor and tenderness.
5.  **Prepare the Grill:** About 30-40 minutes before you plan to cook, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the coals to create two zones: a direct heat zone (coals directly under the cooking grate) and an indirect heat zone (no coals under the grate). Aim for a medium-high heat (around 375-400°F or 190-200°C). Clean and oil the grill grates thoroughly to prevent sticking.
6.  **Grill the Chicken:** Place the marinated chicken pieces over the direct heat zone. Grill for 3-4 minutes per side, rotating frequently, until they develop a nice char and beautiful grill marks. Be careful not to burn them.
7.  **Finish Cooking:** Once charred, move the chicken pieces to the indirect heat zone. Close the grill lid and continue to cook for another 20-30 minutes, or until the internal temperature of the thickest part of the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) and the juices run clear. Turn the chicken occasionally to ensure even cooking.
8.  **Rest and Serve:** Once cooked, remove the Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled from the grill and let it rest for 5-10 minutes. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring maximum succulence.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results
*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. 12-24 hours in the refrigerator will yield the most tender and flavorful Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled. The acidity of the yogurt tenderizes the meat, while the spices infuse deeply.
*   **Use Full-Fat Yogurt:** Full-fat Greek yogurt or hung curd (yogurt with excess whey drained) creates a thicker marinade that clings better to the chicken, preventing it from drying out on the grill.
*   **Score the Chicken Deeply:** The gashes aren't just for show; they allow the marinade to penetrate the meat, ensuring flavor in every bite.
*   **Don't Overcrowd the Grill:** Grill in batches if necessary. Overcrowding lowers the grill temperature and steams the chicken instead of charring it, preventing that beautiful crust.
*   **Monitor Grill Temperature:** Initial high heat for charring, then move to indirect heat to cook through gently. A digital thermometer is your best friend for ensuring the chicken is cooked perfectly without drying out.
*   **Mustard Oil Magic:** A small amount of mustard oil in the marinade adds a distinctive pungent flavor that is characteristic of authentic Indian grilling. If you don't have it, a neutral oil works, but you'll miss a subtle layer of flavor.
*   **Rest Your Chicken:** Just like any grilled meat, letting the Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled rest for a few minutes after cooking ensures the juices redistribute, resulting in a more succulent and flavorful dish.

## Serving Suggestions
Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled is a star dish that deserves equally delightful accompaniments. Serve it piping hot with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice, which brightens the rich flavors. A cooling mint-coriander chutney or a simple cucumber raita (yogurt dip) provides a refreshing contrast to the smoky heat. Don't forget the bread – warm, fluffy naan or roti are perfect for scooping up the tender chicken and any leftover marinade. Sliced red onions and a simple green salad can add a crisp, fresh element to your Indian feast. It's truly a complete meal on its own, or it can be the centerpiece of a larger Indian dinner spread.

## Variations and Substitutions
While the classic Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled is unbeatable, there are many ways to adapt this recipe to suit different preferences or dietary needs:
*   **Chicken Parts:** Instead of a whole chicken, you can use boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, adjusting cooking times accordingly (breasts will cook faster). Drumsticks are also a popular choice.
*   **Vegetarian Options:** The tandoori marinade works wonders on paneer (Indian cheese), mushrooms, cauliflower florets, or even firm tofu, offering delicious vegetarian alternatives. Simply adjust grilling times.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of Kashmiri chili powder to control the heat. For an extra kick, add finely chopped green chilies to the marinade.
*   **No Charcoal Grill?** If you don't have a charcoal grill, you can bake the chicken in a hot oven (400°F/200°C) and finish it under a broiler for charring. A gas grill can also be used, perhaps with a smoker box for added smoky flavor.
*   **Dairy-Free:** For a dairy-free version, use a plant-based yogurt (like coconut or soy yogurt), though the texture and flavor might vary slightly. Ensure it's unsweetened and plain.
*   **Gluten-Free:** The recipe is naturally gluten-free, but always double-check your spice blends and yogurt to ensure no hidden gluten-containing ingredients.

Creating Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled at home is a culinary adventure that promises incredible aromas and even more incredible flavors. With these steps and tips, you're well on your way to mastering this beloved Indian classic and bringing the taste of the tandoor to your own table. Enjoy the process, and savor every smoky, spicy bite!
